label: prf:tower-pair-equality-fixed-level
title: Proof of tower pair equality fixed level
html:
Proof

By the Markov-trace factorization theorem (thm:markov-trace-factorization), the level-n Markov trace of a product of factors decomposes as a sum over subset structures with weights determined by the Markov parameter z. For a pair (i, j) \in \mathcal{P}_n, the two-factor subset contributes the weight z^2 (from prop:markov-pair-z2: \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i \sigma_j) = z \cdot z = z^2, adjacent or not). The dilogarithm \Phi_q applied to the absolute value of the pair product |\hat V_i^{(n)} \hat V_j^{(n)}| is the quantum-dilogarithm regularization of the pair's contribution to the jet-tower mass.

Pair commutativity lem:vhat-pair-commutation-trace ensures the pair index (i, j) vs (j, i) does not double-count (the absolute value |\hat V_i^{(n)} \hat V_j^{(n)}| = |\hat V_j^{(n)} \hat V_i^{(n)}| is symmetric). Summing over \mathcal{P}_n — the set of unordered pairs — gives the level-n pair contribution

  \mathrm{pairs}_n
  \;=\;
  z^2 \sum_{(i, j) \in \mathcal{P}_n}
    \Phi_q\!\bigl(\bigl|\hat V_i^{(n)} \hat V_j^{(n)}\bigr|\bigr),

as an exact equality. \square

Nature of the empirical residual

The empirical table on light atoms (rem:mass-endomorphism-jet-tower §all-pairs vs adjacent error) shows that the all-pairs sum at jet level 0 leaves a sub-1% residual to CODATA — e.g., 0.57\% for ^6\mathrm{Li}, 0.86\% for ^{16}\mathrm{O}. The lemma above says this residual is not a sharpness gap in the level-0 pair formula (the formula is exact at level 0); rather, the residual is the level-\ge 1 contribution of the brane tower not yet captured by the level-0 truncation.

This is consistent with the jet-tower formula (eq:jet-tower-mass):

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  \;=\;
  \underbrace{\bigl|\textstyle\prod_i \hat V_i^{(0)}\bigr|}_{\text{descended (level 0)}}
  + \sum_{n=0}^{N}
      \Bigl(
        \underbrace{\textstyle\sum_i \Phi_q(|\hat V_i^{(n)}|)}_{\text{singletons}_n}
        + \underbrace{z^2 \textstyle\sum_{(i, j) \in \mathcal{P}_n}
            \Phi_q(|\hat V_i^{(n)} \hat V_j^{(n)}|)}_{\text{pairs}_n}
      \Bigr).

Each term is exact at its level; the truncation error at level N is bounded by prop:jet-tower-convergence at \le \Delta_{\max}\,\hbar_q^{2(N+1)} / (1 - \hbar_q^2) once the uniform \Delta_{\max} bound is established (still open).
